issue.title: uniqueItems/enum/const crash with TypeError when input contains object with non-function toString or valueOf property
issue.author: zhangjiashuo-cs

workaround.author: fitzyracing1
workaround.excerpt:
Until this is fixed in ajv, you can work around it by overriding the dependency. I maintain a fork of fast-deep-equal that fixes the `toString`/`valueOf` crashes (plus `Object.create(null)` objects) with the same API:

```json
"overrides": {
  "fast-deep-equal": "npm:@fitzyracing/fast-deep-equal@^3.1.4"
}
```

With that, `uniq([{}, { toString: "" }])` returns `true` instead of throwing. Source and tests: https://github.com/fitzyracing1/fast-deep-equal. I'm the author. Use yarn `resolutions` or pnpm `overrides` for those package managers.

card.condition: Validating with uniqueItems/enum/const throws an uncaught TypeError when the data contains an object whose toString or valueOf property is a non-function value, e.g. [{},{"toString":""}].
card.workaround: Override fast-deep-equal with a patched fork via package.json overrides (e.g. "npm:@fitzyracing/fast-deep-equal@^3.1.4"), or wrap validate() calls in try/catch.

issue.title: Maximum call stack exceeded with 600 oneOf options AND allErrors: true
issue.author: heath-freenome

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv are you using? Does the issue happen if you use the latest version? 8.20.0

card.condition: Compiling a schema whose oneOf has hundreds of branches (e.g. 600 const options) with allErrors: true throws "Maximum call stack size exceeded".
card.workaround: Use a single enum (with titles kept somewhere else) instead of a large oneOf of const branches, or reduce the number of oneOf options.

issue.title: feat: Global additionalProperties validation option
issue.author: luke-perry-ck

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv you are you using? 8.20.0

card.condition: This is a feature request: the reporter wants a new instance-wide additionalProperties option, and it does not describe a defect.
card.workaround: Set additionalProperties in each schema, or use removeAdditional if it's fine for extra properties to be stripped from the data.

issue.title: deepPatternProperties & deepPatternRequired & uniquePatternProperties
issue.author: VivaRado

evidence.quote: On **AJV** version: 8.20.0, we are trying to target **enumerated object keys** with **wildcard pointers**, reasons could include imported/converted **XSD** sche

card.condition: This is a feature request for new keywords (deepPatternProperties, deepPatternRequired, uniquePatternProperties), not a defect.

issue.title: removeAdditional does not work when additionalProperties is not explicitly false
issue.author: preeder

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv are you using? Does the issue happen if you use the latest version? 8.20.0

card.condition: With removeAdditional: true, additional properties are only removed when additionalProperties is literally false, so a schema like additionalProperties: { not: true } leaves them in the data and validation fails.
card.workaround: Use removeAdditional: 'failing' (or 'all'), or set additionalProperties: false.

issue.title: required/properties/dependencies treat Object.prototype property names (toString, constructor, __proto__) as present in the data
issue.author: maximilliangrand

card.condition: Ajv checks whether a property exists with data[prop] !== undefined, so property names that come from Object.prototype (toString, constructor, __proto__, ...) count as present on {}: required lets missing properties through, properties runs subschemas against inherited values, and dependencies fire w
card.workaround: Pass the Ajv option ownProperties: true, which makes Ajv check only own properties.

issue.title: Using $schema to validate against meta-schema is protocol-sensitive. Should it?
issue.author: Kilkenni

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv are you using? 8.20.0

card.condition: A schema whose $schema uses the https URL of a bundled meta-schema (e.g. https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#) throws "no schema with key or ref" because Ajv only registers the http id.
card.workaround: Use the http:// form of the $schema URL (http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#), or register the meta-schema under the https key with addMetaSchema.

issue.title: Own "__proto__" keys are dropped when values are embedded in generated code
issue.author: DanielMcSheehy

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv are you using? Does the issue happen if you use the latest version? 8.20.0, current `master`. Yes.

card.condition: When a schema const, enum or default value has an own "__proto__" key, the generated code embeds it as an object literal. Standalone validators then reject matching data, and with useDefaults the assigned defaults get a prototype set instead of an own "__proto__" key.
card.workaround: Avoid own "__proto__" keys in schema const, enum or default values, or validate in-process instead of with standalone code. The reporter's planned fix is to emit JSON.parse(...) for such values.

issue.title: perf: compare up to 12 property names in additionalProperties
issue.author: DanielMcSheehy

evidence.quote: What version of Ajv you are you using? 8.20.0, current `master`.

card.condition: This is a performance proposal: schemas with 9–12 properties check additionalProperties more slowly because they use hasOwnProperty instead of an === chain.

issue.title: consider removing require-from-string dependency
issue.author: proppy

evidence.quote: Still applies to `ajv@8.20.0`, which continues to depend on `require-from-string@^2.0.2` — a package last published in April 2018 and now flagged End-of-Life by

card.condition: This is a request to remove ajv's require-from-string dependency, which security scanners flag as end-of-life. It is not a defect in how ajv behaves.

issue.title: discriminator rejects schemas whose tag values are Object.prototype member names (toString, constructor, ...)
issue.author: haskiindahouse

evidence.quote: 8.20.0, reproduced on HEAD `f177fe32`. The check is unchanged on `master`.

card.condition: Compiling a schema with discriminator: true throws "values must be unique strings" when any oneOf branch's tag const is an Object.prototype member name such as "toString" or "constructor".
card.workaround: Don't use Object.prototype member names as discriminator tag values, or drop the discriminator keyword and rely on plain oneOf.

issue.title: JTD compileParser rejects valid JSON encodings of enum values (raw byte compare against the JSON.stringify form)
issue.author: haskiindahouse

evidence.quote: 8.20.0, reproduced on HEAD `f177fe32`. `parseEnum` is unchanged on `master`.

card.condition: A JTD parser built by compileParser for an enum schema rejects valid JSON strings that use escapes (\uXXXX, \/), including its own serializer output, because it compares raw bytes against the JSON.stringify form.
card.workaround: Use {type: "string"} in the parser schema and check enum membership yourself after parsing, or decode with JSON.parse and then validate.

issue.title: unevaluatedProperties ignores properties evaluated by $ref when an untaken if/then/else branch has "properties"
issue.author: point-source

workaround.author: point-source
workaround.excerpt: No, I am not planning a PR. The `allOf` wrapping above works as a workaround.

card.condition: With unevaluatedProperties: false, properties evaluated via a sibling $ref are reported as unevaluated when the if/then/else branch that isn't taken contains "properties".
card.workaround: Wrap the if/then/else conditional in an allOf: "allOf": [{ "if": ..., "then": ... }].

issue.title: Strange `humanize` intervals
issue.author: fluffy-critter

card.condition: humanize picks odd granularity thresholds in 1.4.0: for example, 16 days ahead comes out as "in a month" and just under 14 days comes out as "a week".
card.workaround: Use humanize with an explicit granularity (for example granularity="week" or "day"), or compute the relative wording yourself for intervals of a few weeks.

issue.title: dehumanize() silently ignores negative time values, returning wrong results
issue.author: amanv0007

card.condition: dehumanize() drops the minus sign on negative numbers (e.g. "in -1 hours") and returns the same result as the positive value, without raising an error.
card.workaround: Check user input for negative numbers (e.g. a '-' before a digit) and reject it before calling dehumanize().

issue.title: Timezone parsing accepts invalid values
issue.author: number492

card.condition: Arrow's timezone parser accepts malformed offsets like "+03:00.34" as valid when it should reject them.
card.workaround: Check timezone strings yourself, e.g. with a strict regex like ^[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}$, before passing them to arrow.

issue.title: dehumanize() silently returns wrong times for fractional inputs ("1.5 hours ago" is off by 3.5 hours)
issue.author: Mukller

evidence.quote: **Version:** arrow 1.4.0 (release; also on current master). Verified on Python 3.13.

card.condition: dehumanize() with a fractional number like "1.5 hours ago" or "0.5 days ago" splits the number at the decimal point and silently returns the wrong time.
card.workaround: Avoid fractional amounts: convert to whole smaller units (e.g. "90 minutes ago"), or compute the time with shift(hours=-1.5) instead.

issue.title: Quadratic-time ReDoS in Unix-timestamp (X) format token parsing
issue.author: router0mail

card.condition: Calling arrow.get(s, "X") on a long string of digits that doesn't match takes quadratic time because the timestamp regex backtracks, which makes it a ReDoS risk.
card.workaround: Cap the input length, or check it against r"^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?$" before passing it to arrow.get with "X". You can also convert it with float() and use arrow.get(float_value).

issue.title: fetch adapter: response-stream capability probe leaks an uncancelled ReadableStream
issue.author: bdcarr

evidence.quote: axios 1.20.0 (present since the probe was introduced; 1.13.2 leaks both probes)

card.condition: The fetch adapter's supportsResponseStream probe creates new Response('').body and never cancels it, so each module realm (e.g. each test file) leaks a pending ReadableStream promise that async-leak detectors report.
card.workaround: Patch lib/adapters/fetch.js so it keeps a reference to the probe body and cancels it after the capability check, using a best-effort helper that ignores errors from cancel().

issue.title: Axios 1.20.0 fetch adapter still sends inherited headers with ordinary fetchOptions on Node
issue.author: forceworks

evidence.quote: Axios 1.20.0 fetch adapter still sends inherited headers with ordinary fetchOptions on Node

card.condition: With adapter "fetch" on Node and fetchOptions such as cache or redirect (or any options on Node 24), a polluted Object.prototype.headers replaces the caller's headers in the outgoing request, so inherited headers like Authorization get sent.
card.workaround: Use the default Node http adapter instead of adapter: "fetch", or don't pass fetchOptions, and protect against prototype pollution (for example with Object.freeze(Object.prototype)).

issue.title: Nested Buffer fields lose their parent paths in URL-encoded requests
issue.author: imharjot

evidence.quote: Axios 1.20.0, `v1.x` at `c4303eeb601d3d5914a0f425cc7539616fdc7ea7`; Node 24.11.1 on macOS. Reproduced through `axios.post` against a local HTTP echo server.

card.condition: In Node, when axios serializes data as URL-encoded, a Buffer nested inside an object is sent under its bare key and loses its parent path, so first.file and second.file both arrive as 'file'.
card.workaround: Before sending, convert nested Buffers to base64 strings yourself (buf.toString('base64')) so the default visitor keeps their paths.

issue.title: Fetch adapter leaves response open after Content-Length limit rejection
issue.author: IbrahimHafez1

evidence.quote: Axios `v1.x` at `e1a8a57519d1b896c2a795d0ec0138fe24a77a33` (package version 1.20.0); Windows; Node.js 22.17.1 for the original reproduction. The patch was valid

card.condition: With adapter 'fetch', a response whose Content-Length is larger than maxContentLength is rejected with ERR_BAD_RESPONSE, but its unread body is never canceled, so the connection stays open.
card.workaround: Use the http adapter for requests that set maxContentLength, or apply the proposed patch, which cancels response.body when the size limit is exceeded.

issue.title: Node HTTP adapter rejects non-base64 data URLs with non-UTF-8 escapes or a stray %
issue.author: Dev-next-gen

card.condition: With the Node http adapter, a non-base64 data: URL whose body contains a stray % or percent-escapes that aren't valid UTF-8 (e.g. %00%FF) gets rejected with ERR_BAD_REQUEST "URI malformed".
card.workaround: Encode the data: URL body as base64, or use adapter: 'fetch' for data URLs.

issue.title: http adapter: keep-alive sockets retain their last request and response when following redirects (`kAxiosCurrentReq` never cleared)
issue.author: grycuk

card.condition: With the Node http adapter, a keep-alive agent and maxRedirects left at its default, each idle pooled socket holds on to its last RedirectableRequest and that request's full response, because the kAxiosCurrentReq tag is never cleared, so memory is retained.
card.workaround: Set maxRedirects: 0 when redirects aren't needed. Otherwise patch the adapter so it also calls clearCurrentReq when the response emits 'close'.

issue.title: Node http adapter drops the filename of FormData files with an empty name, so they arrive as text fields
issue.author: Dev-next-gen

card.condition: With the Node http adapter, a FormData file entry appended with an empty filename is sent without a filename parameter, so the server receives it as a text field and corrupts binary bytes.
card.workaround: Give the file entry a non-empty filename when appending it to FormData.

issue.title: Node HTTP adapter fails to decode deflate responses made with a zlib window smaller than 32K
issue.author: Dev-next-gen

card.condition: In Node, axios's HTTP adapter fails with Z_DATA_ERROR on a Content-Encoding: deflate response whose zlib stream uses a window smaller than 32K (first byte is not 0x78), because it adds a second zlib header in front of it.
card.workaround: Set decompress: false and use responseType 'arraybuffer', then decode the body yourself with zlib.inflateSync.

issue.title: `AxiosError.prototype.toJSON()` can OOM when config includes an `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent`
issue.author: skrtheboss

evidence.quote: No heap exhaustion and the serialized payload stays bounded. Could you retest on v1.20.0? If you still see unbounded growth in your setup, a standalone repro (a

card.condition: AxiosError.toJSON() deep-serializes config.httpAgent/httpsAgent internals, so it can blow up memory and run the process out of heap when many failed requests share one agent.
card.workaround: Upgrade to v1.20.0 or later (fixed by #11141). On older versions, don't call error.toJSON() when the request uses an agent; log only the fields you need.

issue.title: AxiosHeaders set() never calls a rewrite function, so the header is never overwritten
issue.author: Prafyl

evidence.quote: this is on 1.20.0 and v2.x has the same check. has() and delete() already take the same kind of matcher through matchHeaderValue, so set() should probably do th

card.condition: AxiosHeaders#set (and accessors like setContentType) treat a function, string or RegExp rewrite argument as false, so the existing header is never overwritten and the matcher is never called.
card.workaround: Evaluate the matcher yourself against headers.get(name), then call set(name, value, true) when it matches.

issue.title: Progress throttle crashes with "args is not iterable" when the trailing timer fires after flush (setTimeout wrapped by third-party code)
issue.author: jelle-eastground

card.condition: The progress throttle's trailing timer calls invoke(null) and throws an uncaught "args is not iterable" TypeError after a request finishes. This happens when third-party code has replaced window.setTimeout with a wrapper that does not return the real timer id.
card.workaround: The thread has no app-level workaround. The suggested library fix is to patch lib/helpers/throttle.js so the timer callback does `lastArgs && invoke(lastArgs)`, matching what flush() already does.

issue.title: `click.edit` on Windows throws WinError 14001 or 87
issue.author: emorynb

card.condition: On some Windows 11 systems, click.edit() launching notepad intermittently fails with WinError 87 or 14001, apparently due to a Windows app-alias bug.
card.workaround: Set the editor explicitly with editor=... (for example a non-Store editor) or retry when it fails.

issue.title: Click 9.0
issue.author: Rowlando13

notes: title is about a different version

workaround.author: davidism
workaround.excerpt: See https://github.com/di/pyreadiness/issues/18 for my reasons not to use python version classifiers.Please drop this line of conversation, it's not changing. Click supports Python 3.14, no pinning to main required. If you find a bug with 3.14, report a bug.

issue.title: zh-CN cannot parse its own formatted quarter: localize produces 季 forms but match expects 刻 forms
issue.author: cozuya

evidence.quote: - date-fns: reproduced against current `main`, and the published date-fns@4.4.0 on npm contains the same `matchQuarterPatterns`.

card.condition: With the zhCN locale, parse() using the QQQ/QQQQ tokens returns Invalid Date for the 季 quarter strings that format() itself produces, because the match patterns only accept the 刻 forms.
card.workaround: Before parsing, swap 季度→刻钟 and 季→刻 in the input string, or parse the quarter number yourself instead of relying on zhCN's QQQ/QQQQ parsing.

issue.title: formatDistanceStrict / formatDistanceToNowStrict return "60 seconds", "60 minutes" and "24 hours" instead of promoting to the next unit when rounding
issue.author: philppplik

card.condition: With the default 'round' (or 'ceil') roundingMethod, durations just below a unit boundary (e.g. 59.5s, 59m59.5s, 23h59m59.5s) format as "60 seconds", "60 minutes" or "24 hours" instead of "1 minute", "1 hour" or "1 day".
card.workaround: Pass roundingMethod: 'floor', or use the non-strict formatDistance.

issue.title: "preprocessor" undefined
issue.author: Vishwas-93

evidence.quote: It would great if this issue could be resolved - it's still evident in v4.4.0

card.condition: format with a locale loaded via require("date-fns/locale/xx") (module namespace rather than the locale object) crashes reading "preprocessor" of undefined localize.
card.workaround: Import the named locale, e.g. `import { de } from "date-fns/locale"`, instead of require("date-fns/locale/de").

issue.title: Calendar callbacks ignore an explicit referenceTime
issue.author: kazuki-netizen

evidence.quote: Install `dayjs@1.11.23`, save this as `repro.cjs`, and run `TZ=UTC node repro.cjs`:

card.condition: When calendar(referenceTime, formats) is given function callbacks, the callback gets the current system time as its argument instead of the referenceTime you passed in.
card.workaround: Inside the callback, use the reference value from the enclosing scope (a closure) instead of the callback's argument.

issue.title: [Regression in 1.11.22] Instance .tz() breaks when Intl.DateTimeFormat.prototype.formatToParts is missing or unreliable
issue.author: QuentinRoadstr

card.condition: Since 1.11.22, instance .tz() relies on Intl.DateTimeFormat formatToParts. On runtimes where formatToParts is missing or unreliable (React Native Hermes on iOS), it throws a TypeError or returns an absurd offset, so dates shift by a day.
card.workaround: Pin dayjs to 1.11.21, or polyfill Intl.DateTimeFormat.prototype.formatToParts correctly (for example with @formatjs/intl-datetimeformat) on Hermes.

issue.title: Built `locale/ku.js` exports a wrapper object, not the locale
issue.author: akamfoad

card.condition: Importing or requiring dayjs/locale/ku returns a wrapper object { default, englishToArabicNumbersMap } instead of the locale, so dayjs.locale(ku) has no effect in CJS, Node ESM, or Vite 8.
card.workaround: Use require('dayjs/locale/ku').default (or the .default of the imported module), or import the 'ku' side effect and call dayjs.locale('ku') by name.

issue.title: duration plugin: leading sign of an ISO 8601 duration is ignored ("-P1D" parses as +1 day)
issue.author: philppplik

card.condition: dayjs.duration() parsing an ISO 8601 string with a leading minus sign (e.g. '-P1D') ignores the sign and returns a positive duration, which also breaks round-trips from toISOString() of negative durations.
card.workaround: Strip a leading '-' yourself and negate the result, e.g. s.startsWith('-') ? dayjs.duration(-dayjs.duration(s.slice(1)).asMilliseconds()) : dayjs.duration(s).

issue.title: fix localized format for `cs` locale
issue.author: Iaotle

card.condition: With the cs locale, format('LL'/'LLL'/'LLLL') or 'D. MMMM YYYY' outputs the nominative month name (říjen) where Czech grammar needs the genitive (října).
card.workaround: Use updateLocale to give cs a months function that returns the genitive names when the format string has a day before MMMM, as moment does.

issue.title: Timezone startOf DST off-by-one
issue.author: ashconnell

evidence.quote: I can reproduce this on 1.11.23, and it depends on the system time zone, which may be why it's hard to pin down. With the system zone in America/Vancouver (same

card.condition: When the date was created with dayjs.tz, startOf('day') on a date whose offset differs from the current offset (across a DST change) uses the wrong offset and returns the previous day at 23:00.
card.workaround: Upgrade to a release that includes PR #1352 (1.10.5 or later).

issue.title: Impossible to set time that don't exist in browser timezone in another timezone (during daylight saving change)
issue.author: baptistegaut

evidence.quote: This also breaks plain conversions, not only setting a time. On dayjs 1.11.23 with the system zone in America/Vancouver (same results in Chrome, Firefox, Safari

card.condition: When the shifted wall-clock time in the target timezone or offset falls in a DST gap of the system's local timezone, tz() or utcOffset() moves the time by an hour, which gives the wrong instant or the wrong displayed hour.

issue.title: +00:00 timezone bug
issue.author: janousek

evidence.quote: Confirmed this still reproduces in **Day.js 1.11.23** (current npm latest), as well as **1.11.13**, through the public `dayjs.tz(string, zone)` API. Here is a m

card.condition: When the host timezone's offset is 0 (for example Europe/London in winter, Europe/Lisbon or UTC+0), the utc plugin's valueOf uses `$localOffset || getTimezoneOffset()`, so the valid 0 offset is thrown away. dayjs.tz(string, zone) and utcOffset then return instants that are off by an hour near DST ch
card.workaround: Run the process with TZ=UTC. Another option is to patch utc/index.js so it checks `$localOffset` with `??` (nullish) instead of `||` (PR #1678).

issue.title: diff(..., 'year'|'month', true) returns 0 instead of NaN for an Invalid Date operand
issue.author: yfwmaniish

evidence.quote: Confirmed on 1.11.23, and your read of `monthDiff` is right. `invalid.diff(now, 'month'|'year', true)` returns `0`, while `'day'`/`'hour'` return `NaN` because

card.condition: When either operand is an Invalid Date, diff(other, 'month'|'year') returns 0 instead of NaN, because monthDiff's trailing `|| 0` turns NaN into 0.
card.workaround: Check isValid() on both dates before calling diff with month/year units, or patch monthDiff to end with `+ 0` instead of `|| 0`.

issue.title: Add days across Daylight Saving Time
issue.author: MarkSFrancis

evidence.quote: Rechecked the original example with Day.js 1.11.23 on Node 24.19.0 / ICU 78.3. With host `TZ=UTC`, `America/Santiago`, `America/New_York` or `Asia/Shanghai`, th

workaround.author: moulinraphael

issue.title: Missing type annotation for FILTERS
issue.author: Gabgobie

card.condition: Environment.filters is reported as partially unknown by static type checkers because FILTERS has no type annotation; nothing goes wrong at runtime.
card.workaround: Annotate or cast the filters dict locally, for example cast(dict[str, Callable[..., Any]], env.filters).

issue.title: TypeError: cannot use 'tuple' as a dict key in LRUCache on Python 3.14
issue.author: baconisgood99-ship-it

workaround.author: tk1475
workaround.excerpt: I don't think this is a Jinja or Python 3.14 problem. Starlette 1.0.0 dropped the old `TemplateResponse(name, {"request": request})` call style (Kludex/starlette#3118), so the signature is now `TemplateResponse(request, name, context)`. With an old-style call, the dict is passed as `name`, and Jinja builds its cache key as `(weakref.ref(self.loader), name)`, which can't be hashed. Setting `env.cache = None` only hides it because the cache lookup is skipped. The fix is to call `templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", {...})`. fastapi/fastapi#15197 is the same report from the FastAPI side.

card.condition: With Starlette 1.0, calling TemplateResponse(name, {"request": request}) in the old style passes the context dict as the template name, so Jinja's cache-key hashing raises TypeError.
card.workaround: Call templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", {...}) using the new argument order.

issue.title: ChainableUndefined causes `is escaped` test to pass for `undefined` child elements
issue.author: colinrotherham

workaround.author: colinrotherham

card.condition: With undefined=ChainableUndefined, the template test `x is escaped` returns true for undefined values (e.g. missing child attributes) because ChainableUndefined defines __html__.
card.workaround: Guard the test with `is defined`, e.g. `parent.child is defined and parent.child is escaped`.

issue.title: test_elif_deep sometimes fail with RecursionError
issue.author: frenzymadness

card.condition: Compiling a template with a very long if/elif chain (about 1000 elifs) sometimes fails with "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded during compilation" in Python's compile() on Python 3.12 and 3.13.
card.workaround: Avoid very long elif chains in templates. For example, use a dict lookup or a loop instead.

issue.title: Unable to combine the map and sort filters using the async renderer
issue.author: ogenstad

workaround.author: ogenstad
workaround.excerpt:
As a workaround changing the template to look like this makes it work on both of the variants:

```python
template_str = """
sorted_letters={{ letters
    | map(attribute='value')
    | list
    | sort
 }}
"""
```

card.condition: With enable_async=True, a template that pipes map(...) straight into sort raises TypeError: 'async_generator' object is not iterable, because sort does not support async iterables.
card.workaround: Put a `| list` filter between map and sort, e.g. `letters | map(attribute='value') | list | sort`.

issue.title: Accessing a variable has unexpected side effects on visit_Name for custom Extension
issue.author: 502E532E

card.condition: A custom extension that emits nodes.OverlayScope with a context expression naming a template variable fails with an AssertionError ("Tried to resolve a name to a reference that was unknown to the frame") unless that variable was already referenced earlier in the template.
card.workaround: Reference the variable earlier in the template (e.g. {{- a -}}) so the frame resolves it before the OverlayScope.

issue.title: poor performance when parsing unclosed string with many escape characters
issue.author: wsparks-vc

card.condition: Lexing a template source that contains an unclosed quoted string with many backslash escapes takes super-linear time because the string_re regex backtracks.
card.workaround: Don't compile untrusted template sources. If you must, cap the input size and enforce a timeout or resource limits.

issue.title: Slice returns one extra item when slice count is a divisor of iterable length and fill_with not none
issue.author: matiasilva

card.condition: The slice filter with a fill_with value adds an extra fill item to every slice when the slice count evenly divides the sequence length.
card.workaround: Don't pass fill_with when the length is evenly divisible by the slice count, or pad the slices yourself.

issue.title: `test_elif_deep` fails on s390x with `RecursionError`
issue.author: amaanq

card.condition: The test suite's test_elif_deep, which builds 999 nested elif branches, raises RecursionError on s390x with CPython 3.12/3.13 because the C recursion limit is lower there.
card.workaround: Lower the depth used in the test, or use CPython 3.14.

issue.title: `[{}] | map(attribute = "foo", default = None)` still fails
issue.author: westhand

card.condition: The map filter called with attribute=... and default=none ignores the default and raises an undefined-attribute error for items missing that attribute, because None is treated as "no default given".
card.workaround: Pass a sentinel default that isn't None (for example default="") and convert it afterwards, or chain the default filter on each element instead of using map's default.

issue.title: `indent` filter ignores `blank`=`False` when `first`=`True` on first line
issue.author: abstract-official

card.condition: indent(first=True) adds indentation to an empty or blank first line even when blank=False, so empty content renders as stray spaces.
card.workaround: Drop first=True and put the indent filter's start somewhere the first line is already indented, or don't indent the first line yourself. Another option is to strip the output when the content is empty.

issue.title: Fixing Knex's GROUP BY Parameter Duplication Issue
issue.author: mercmobily

workaround.author: mercmobily
workaround.excerpt:
- Gives users immediate workarounds

**Cons:**
- Requires users to change their code
- Doesn't fix existing code automatically
- Multiple ways to do the same thing (API complexity)

Implement **Solution #5 (New API Methods)** first:
- Ship in next minor version (e.g., 3.2.0)
- Provides immediate workarounds for affected users
- Fully backwards compatible
- Clear migration path

Example implementation:
```javascript

knex('users')
  .select(knex.raw('??#>>?', ['attributes', ['job']]).as('job_field'))
  .groupByAlias('job_field')  // New!

// Or with expression tracking

knex('users')
  .select(jobExpr.as('job'))
  .groupBy(jobExpr)  // Reuses same parameters
```

issue.title: BUG: SIGSEGV when creating an array from a deeply nested structured dtype
issue.author: eGkritsis

workaround.author: ngoldbaum
workaround.excerpt:
Here is a reproducer that crashes on `main` on any system. The reproducer in the issue description relies on Linux-specific details and passes on my Mac.

```python
import threading
import numpy as np

def main():
    dt = np.dtype([("v", "i4")])
    for _ in range(50_000):
        dt = np.dtype([("v", "i4"), ("next", dt)])
    np.zeros(1, dtype=dt)

# 1 MiB thread stack
threading.stack_size(1 << 20)
t = threading.Thread(target=main)
t.start()
t.join()
print("no crash")
```

The fix is to add `Py_EnterRecursiveCall` guards to C internals that are triggering the overflows. This should be happening everywhere we do recursion in C.

issue.title: `extend` and `scatter` corrupt Boolean values and nulls of an offset slice
issue.author: taozuoqiao

workaround.author: taozuoqiao
workaround.excerpt:
### Workaround

Gathering every row gives the target fresh buffers, including validity:

```python
t = t.select(pl.all().gather(pl.int_range(pl.len())))
```

A Boolean cast round trip is not enough for nullable columns, because the cast keeps the offset validity.

### Installed versions

```
Polars:     2.0.0 (build 22a147de3d2bb2e44b97338a2510816c7105c9f2)
Index type: UInt32
Platform:   Linux x86_64, glibc 2.34
Python:     3.12.15
Optional dependencies: none installed
```

Also reproduced on 1.42.0, 1.42.1, 1.43.2 and 1.44.1.

AI disclosure: investigated with Claude Code and Codex; the examples and the source reading were checked by me.

card.condition: Calling extend or scatter on a uniquely owned Boolean Series/DataFrame that is an offset slice (e.g. from slice or filter keeping a suffix) corrupts the existing values and null positions, because the bitmap is read from bit 0.
card.workaround: Give the target fresh buffers before extending, e.g. t = t.select(pl.all().gather(pl.int_range(pl.len()))), or keep a reference to the parent alive.

issue.title: [Python] Table.from_pandas() zero-copy numeric columns are not protected by pandas 3.0 Copy-on-Write
issue.author: tritsystem

evidence.quote: pyarrow 25.0.1, pandas 3.0.5 (Copy-on-Write unconditional/default since 3.0), Python 3.12.10, Windows 11. Confirmed present in `pyarrow/pandas_compat.py` on `ma

workaround.author: Diveyam-Mishra
workaround.excerpt:
Thanks for filing this with a clean repro. I was able to reproduce and test this behavior across Pandas 2.2 / 3.0.
Under the hood, this is a known design limitation in Pandas' Copy-on-Write architecture regarding external/third-party zero-copy consumers:
Immediate Workaround: PyArrow Backend

For users looking for guaranteed buffer independence and immutability under CoW today, using the PyArrow backend in Pandas completely avoids this issue:
```python
# Using PyArrow-backed dtypes
df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]}, dtype="int64[pyarrow]")
table = pa.Table.from_pandas(df)

df.iloc[0, 0] = 999

print(table.column("a").to_pylist())  # [1, 2, 3]
print(df["a"].to_list())             # [999, 2,
```
…

card.condition: Table.from_pandas() wraps a non-null numeric column's numpy buffer without copying, so a later in-place cell edit on the source DataFrame (df.iloc/df.loc assignment) silently changes the Table's data, even with pandas 3.0 Copy-on-Write.
card.workaround: Use pyarrow-backed dtypes in the DataFrame (e.g. dtype="int64[pyarrow]"), or pass df.copy() to from_pandas before you mutate the DataFrame.

issue.title: [BUG] Text.from_ansi leaves empty lines when input string has CRLF line endings
issue.author: kaipons

workaround.author: Yad4o
workaround.excerpt:
Hi, I've reproduced this and traced it to the `decode()` method in `rich/ansi.py`.

The split regex `(?<=\n)` keeps `\n` at end of each chunk, which `decode_line` strips with `rstrip("\n")`. But on CRLF input (`\r\n`), the `\r` remains — and then `line.rsplit("\r", 1)[-1]` takes only what's **after** the last `\r`, which is empty, producing blank lines.

The fix is a one-liner in `decode()`: strip `\r` from each line before passing to `decode_line`:

```python
# current
for line in re.split(r"(?<=\n)", terminal_text):
    yield self.decode_line(line.rstrip("\n"))

# fixed
for line in re.split(r"(?<=\n)", terminal_text):
    yield self.decode_line(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
```
…

card.condition: In rich 15.0.0, Text.from_ansi (or AnsiDecoder.decode) on input with CRLF line endings returns empty lines, so all the text is lost.
card.workaround: Convert CRLF to LF before decoding, e.g. Text.from_ansi(s.replace("\r\n", "\n")).

issue.title: [BUG] Line breaking breaks at NBSP (U+00A0) — doesn't respect non-breaking space semantics
issue.author: cdxjcl

workaround.author: Mukller
workaround.excerpt:
Root cause confirmed: `re_word = re.compile(r"\s*\S+\s*")` in `rich/_wrap.py`.

In Python's Unicode regex mode, `\s` includes U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE, so `\S` excludes it. This means NBSP is treated as a word separator and therefore a line-break opportunity — directly violating its Unicode semantics.

**Fix:** replace `\s` with `[^\S\u00a0]` (whitespace but not NBSP) and `\S` with `[\S\u00a0]` (non-whitespace or NBSP):

```python
# before
re_word = re.compile(r"\s*\S+\s*")
# after
re_word = re.compile(r"[^\S\u00a0]*[\S\u00a0]+[^\S\u00a0]*")
```

I have a fix ready in a PR.

card.condition: Rich's word-wrapping treats NBSP (U+00A0) as whitespace and wraps lines at it, which splits text that was meant to stay together.
card.workaround: Patch rich._wrap.re_word to r"[^\S\xa0]*[\S\xa0]+[^\S\xa0]*", or pass no_wrap/overflow for that text.

print("1 - ncf.cdf:          ", 1 - ncf.cdf(x, dfn=dfn, dfd=dfd, nc=nc))
print("f.sf:                 ", f.sf(x, dfn=dfn, dfd=dfd))
